fact: 1905年11月17日《日韩协约》（乙巳条约）在汉城签订：日本外务省此后掌握朝鲜对外关系与事务，日本外交领事代表在外国保护朝鲜臣民与利益；朝鲜政府非经日本政府不得缔结任何具有国际性质的 act 或约定；日本驻朝鲜皇帝朝廷设统监，驻汉城并有权随时入觐。条约由林权助与外部大臣朴齐纯签署。

sources.title: CONVENTION. (Convention between Japan and Korea, 1905)，The World and Japan 数据库（田中明彦主编，GRIPS/东大IASA），源出《旧条约纂》第3卷 pp.204-207
sources.quote: ARTICLE I. The Government of Japan, through the Department of Foreign Affairs at Tokyo, will hereafter have control and direction of the external relations and affairs of Corea, and the diplomatic and consular representatives of Japan will have the charge of the subjects and interests of Corea in foreign countries. ARTICLE II. The Government of Japan undertake to see to the execution of the treaties actually existing between Corea and other Powers, and the Government of Corea engage not to conclude hereafter any act or engagement having an international character except through the medium of the Government of Japan. ARTICLE III. The Government of Japan shall be represented at the Court of His Majesty the Emperor of Corea by a Resident General, who shall reside at Seoul...

sources.title: Fred A. McKenzie, Korea's Fight for Freedom (1920; Project Gutenberg eBook #13368)
sources.quote: In the early hours of the morning commands were issued that the seal of State should be brought from the Foreign Minister's apartment, and a treaty should be signed. Here another difficulty arose. The custodian of the seal had received orders in advance that, even if his master commanded, the seal was not to be surrendered for any such purpose. When telephonic orders were sent to him, he refused to bring the seal along, and special messengers had to be despatched to take it from him by force. The Emperor himself asserts to this day that he did not consent.

fact: 1907年7月24日《日韩协约》（丁未条约）在汉城签订，共六条：朝鲜政府非经统监事前同意不得制定法令条例、不得采取重要行政措施；所有高级官员任免须统监协同；朝鲜政府须任命统监推荐的日本人为官员；非经统监协同不得雇佣外国人；1905年8月22日议定书第一条自此失效。由统监伊藤博文与总理大臣李完用签署。

sources.title: Agreement. (Agreement between Japan and Korea, 1907)，The World and Japan 数据库，源出《旧条约纂》第3卷（朝鲜·琉球）pp.212-214
sources.quote: ARTICLE I. The Government of Corea shall act under the guidance of the Resident-General in respect to reforms in administration. ARTICLE II. The Government of Corea engage{sic} not to enact any laws, ordinances or regulations, nor to take any important measures of administration without the previous assent of the Resident-General. ... ARTICLE VI. The Government of Corea shall not engage any foreigner without the concurrence of the Resident-General. ARTICLE VII. Article I of the Protocol between Japan and Corea signed on the 22nd of August, 1905, shall hereafter cease to be binding.

sources.title: Fred A. McKenzie, Korea's Fight for Freedom (Project Gutenberg eBook #13368)
sources.quote: In less than a week the Japanese had prepared a new treaty, providing still more strictly for the absolute control of everything in the country by Japan. The six curt clauses of this measure were as far-reaching as they could possibly be made. No laws were to be acted upon or important measures taken by the Government unless the consent and approval of the Resident-General had been previously given. All officials were to hold their positions at the pleasure of the Resident-General, and the Government of Korea agreed to appoint any Japanese the Resident-General might recommend to any post. Finally, the Government of Korea was to engage no foreigner without the consent of the Japanese head.

fact: 依据1907年7月协定及1907年12月27日公布的法院组织规章，朝鲜设立大法院1所、上诉院3所、地方法院8所、区法院112所，主审法官、检察官与书记由合格日本臣民充任；因法律编纂与人选、建筑准备不足，新法院推迟至1908年8月1日开幕：大法院设汉城，上诉院分设汉城、平壤、大邱，首期先开地方法院8所与重要地区区法院16所。

sources.title: Annual Report on Reforms and Progress in Chosen (1907-1922)，朝鲜总督府官房统计课，Wikimedia Commons 存档扫描本（1909年刊，报道截至1908-09年进度；本条据第73页 OCR）
sources.quote: as a result of the Agreement concluded in July 1907 and by the organic regulations of the various law courts, issued on December 27, there were established a Supreme Court, 3 Courts of Appeal, 8 Local Courts and 112 District Courts throughout the country. Qualified Japanese subjects are to be appointed as principal justices, prosecutors and clerks. These new courts, in accordance with the provisions of the regulations, were to be opened on or after January, 1908. But owing to difficulties connected with the revision or compilation of various laws, ordinances, and operative regulations, as well as with the selection of the various justices, the erection of the Courts' buildings and other preparations, the opening had to be postponed till August 1st of that year. The Supreme Court in Seoul; three Appeal Courts, in Seoul, Pying-yang and Taiku, respectively; 8 Local Courts one each in Seoul and seven other places where Provincial Governments are located, and 16 District Courts out of 112 in the important Districts, were opened as the first stage.

fact: 1908年8月19日公布法律：为鼓励外国资本投资朝鲜矿业开发，对开采金（含砂金）、银、铜所需机械、器具、炸药与化学品免征进口税，对铜及金、银、铜精矿免征出口税——这是保护国时期明确以立法吸引外资进入矿业的产业准入变化。

sources.title: Annual Report on Reforms and Progress in Chosen (1907-1922)，Wikimedia Commons 存档（第111页 OCR：Customs Tariff 节）
sources.quote: In order to encourage the investment of foreign capital in mining development in Korea, import duties on machinery, instruments, explosives and chemicals necessary for mining gold (including placer gold), silver or copper, and export duties on copper and concentrates of gold, silver or copper, have been abolished by a law promulgated on August 19, 1908.

fact: 第一银行（Dai-Ichi Ginko）汉城支店自1905年起经朝鲜政府依日本政府推荐授权为朝鲜中央银行；其朝鲜纸币流通额1907年底为12,805,300圆、1908年底降至10,385,900圆（约减250万圆），原因包括1907年底海外金融紧张与内地骚乱；1907年起停发50、20、10钱小面额券；因日式设计与行长像引起朝鲜民众误解，1圆券于1908年8月改为朝鲜国家徽章图案；设立新朝鲜中央银行的协定于1909年7月2日签订。

sources.title: Annual Report on Reforms and Progress in Chosen (1907-1922)，Wikimedia Commons 存档（第124-125页 OCR：New Coins and Bank Notes / The Dai-Ichi Ginko 节）
sources.quote: As to bank-notes, their issue, also, by the Dai-Ichi Ginko gradually increased with the financial and economic growth of the Peninsula. But the amount of bank-notes circulating in 1908 decreased by about 2½ millions as compared with the figure for the preceding year, owing to financial stringency abroad towards the end of 1907, and owing also to the prevalence of insurrection in the interior. ... Since 1907, the issue of banknotes of small denominations, as 50, 20 and 10 sen was suspended. Moreover, as the notes hitherto issued by the Dai-Ichi Ginko, bearing a Japanese design and a portrait of the President of the Bank, were causing frequent misunderstanding among ignorant Koreans, the one yen, 5-yen and 10-yen notes were replaced by notes carrying the Korean national emblems and designs, in August 1908, January 1909 and July 1909, respectively. ... The last Annual Report shows that the branch office of the Dai-Ichi Ginko (formerly the First National Bank) of Japan in Seoul was authorised, by the Korean Government, on the recommendation of the Japanese Government, to act as the central bank of Korea from 1905. ... an agreement relative to the establishment of the new Central Bank of Korea, was concluded on July 2, 1909.

fact: 1908年前后朝鲜日常交易货币环境剧变：旧铜钱因妨碍交易被逐步收回，至1908年12月21日以兑换、缴纳公款方式收回并输出境外的铜钱累计2,121,121圆（其中1907年1,140,918圆、1908年302,418圆）；1908年6月敕令将铜钱流通价值固定为2厘、并承认为1圆以下之法偿；1905年起被朝鲜政府承认为法偿的日本硬币与纸币随新币制推行逐步退出，1908年底在朝日本硬币流通约338,000圆、日本银行券约199,400圆。穿越者在朝交易需以新币制与圆计价为主，零钱找换环境与战前不同。

sources.quote: Up to December 21, 1908, the amount of copper cash withdrawn by exchange or receipt in payment of public dues and exported abroad, reached 2,121,121 yen. ... the circulating value of the cash was fixed by an Imperial Ordinance in June, 1908, at 2 rin, ... and it was recognized as legal tender up to the value of one yen. ... Finally the Japanese coins and paper money which had been recognized as legal tender throughout Korea by the Korean Government since 1905, gradually went out of circulation as the new Korean currency came into vogue. The amount of Japanese money circulating in Korea at the end of December, each year since 1905 ... 1908: Japanese coins 338,000; Bank-notes 199,400.

fact: 1908年朝鲜对外贸易（不含金银）：输入41,025,523圆、输出14,113,310圆、合计55,138,833圆，较1907年（合计58,361,114圆）减少3,222,281圆；入超26,912,213圆。输入受日朝政治经济关系牵引：日本政府每年花费2,500万至3,000万圆维持统监府、驻军、铁路、邮电等或贷予朝鲜政府；日本居民与外国传教士增加亦推高输入。棉纱、本棉布等朝鲜人消费品输入因朝鲜购买力下降与日本金融紧张减少逾250万圆；中国夏布需求上升，据称已完全取代昔日的曼彻斯特细布；煤炭输入因铁路需求增长逾60%。

sources.title: Annual Report on Reforms and Progress in Chosen (1907-1922)，Wikimedia Commons 存档（第138-139页 OCR：Foreign Commerce 节）
sources.quote: The total value of merchandize imported and exported for the year 1908, exclusive of specie, aggregated 55,138,833 yen, against 58,361,114 yen for the preceding year, showing a decrease of 3,222,281 yen. ... As to the balance of trade, the imports for 1908 exceeded the exports by 26,912,213 yen. ... The imports were greatly influenced by the political and economic relations with Japan, as from 25 to 30 millions were annually spent by the Japanese Government in maintaining the Residency General, the garrison Army, the railways, the posts and the telegraphs, etc., or lent to the Korean Government. In addition, an increase in the number of Japanese residents and foreign missionaries, is to some extent responsible for the excess of imports. ... The demand for grass-cloth is increasing. This fabric, owing to its cheapness, is said to have "entirely ousted Manchester lawns, which formerly were in fair demand" in Korea. An increase of over 60 per cent. in the import of coal is due to the growth of railway requirements

fact: 统监府初期的交通建设：釜山至汉城铁路已建成，汉城至 Wi-ju（通往满洲边境方向）的干线铁路在建，可将日军约三十六小时内自日本本土经朝鲜运抵满洲边境；另有汉城至元山（Gensan，东海岸）铁路建成；以朝鲜海关为担保借入1,000万圆贷款，其中150万圆用于连接主要地区与港口、铁路枢纽的四条军事干线公路，公路按可快速铺设铁轨、通行炮兵与弹药车的标准修筑，部分费用由贷款、部分由特别地方税承担。

sources.title: Fred A. McKenzie, Korea's Fight for Freedom (Project Gutenberg eBook #13368)
sources.quote: The first steps under the new administration were in the direction of perfecting communications throughout the country, so as to enable the troops to be moved easily and rapidly from point to point. A railway had already been built from Fusan to Seoul, and another was in course of completion from Seoul to Wi-ju, thus giving a trunk line that would carry large numbers of Japanese soldiers from Japan itself to the borders of Manchuria in about thirty-six hours. A loan of 10,000,000 yen was raised on the guarantee of the Korean Customs, and a million and a half of this was spent on four main military roads, connecting some of the chief districts with the principal harbours and railway centres. Part of the cost of these roads was paid by the loan and part by special local taxation. It may be pointed out that these roads were military rather than industrial undertakings. ... The new roads were finely graded, and were built in such a manner that rails could be quickly laid down on them and artillery and ammunition wagons rapidly conveyed from point to point. Another railway was built from Seoul to Gensan, on the east coast.

fact: 美国驻汉城总领事Sammons在1909年7月《月度领事与贸易报告》中转引朝鲜政府财务局的估计：朝鲜本地人口9,583,346人中约3,876,033人为烟草消费者，年消费烟草49,478,997磅，每名消费者年均烟草支出约80美分（金币计价）；烟草以本地生产为主，约20%的朝鲜女性吸烟；另有价值约60万美元的外国卷烟每年在朝鲜销售（日本约占其一半进口）。按1908年前后约2日元兑1美元的汇价，80美分约合1.6日元/年——可作保护国城市底层小额嗜好品支出的一项参照。

sources.title: Monthly Consular and Trade Reports, July 1909, No. 346（美国商务部制造局，政府印刷局），Korea—An Extensive Tobacco...一节，govinfo存档扫描PDF（61st Congress, 2d Session, House of Representatives Document No. 151）
sources.quote: KOREA. AN EXTENSIVE TOBACCO Consul-General Thomas Sammons, at Seoul, quotes the financial bureau of the Korean government estimates that of Korea's native population of 9,583,346, a total of 3,876,033 are tobacco smokers, consuming annually 49,478,997 pounds of tobacco at an estimated cost of 80 cents for each smoker. The tobacco used is mostly of native production, and probably 20 per cent of the Korean women are smokers. Approximately $600,000 worth of foreign cigarettes are sold each year in Korea. Japan contributes about 50 per cent of these imports
